claim: For 1B models, the PaLM FLOP formula gives 11.6e20 FLOPs at 8K context and 25.5e20 at 32K - a 2.20x ratio - and the measured training time tracks the FLOPs saving within about 5%, confirming that wall-clock scales with the FLOPs formula at roughly constant MFU for a 1B model.
stance_target: the validity of the 6N+12LHQT FLOPs model as a wall-clock proxy at 1B scale, 8K-32K
scope_conditions: 1B models pretrained on 100B tokens, up to 32K context; FLOPs calculation follows Zhang et al. (TinyLlama)

claim: Naively training a 1B model at a constant 32K context costs 2.20x the FLOPs of a constant 8K run, and scheduling the context window recovers 22% of that training time while improving long-context performance.
stance_target: the size of the long-context training penalty at 1B scale
quoted_support: With a 32K context window, the efficiency gain becomes even more pronounced: our method saves 22% of training time while achieving better performance. The FLOPs saving is larger than the actual time because of reduced attention calculation.

claim: SkyLadder's ablations use 120M models at 8K on 100B tokens, and its main runs are 1B (up to 32K) and 3B (8K) on 100B tokens - the closest published budget match to a small-box 9B-token run is therefore still 11x larger.
stance_target: the token-budget gap between published long-context runs and the box's 9B plan
scope_conditions: 100B tokens for main runs, 100B CC tokens for 120M ablations
quoted_support: we pretrain 1B-parameter models (up to 32K context) and 3B-parameter models (8K context) on 100B tokens ... we adopt a default setup of pretraining 120M models with 8K context on 100B CC tokens.
